interest: For historians of the Allied Occupation of Japan, this document provides concrete insight into SCAP's commercial diplomacy and trade strategies during early post-war economic reconstruction. It illustrates how occupied Japan engaged in bilateral barter transactions—exchanging manufactured textiles such as cotton and rayon for raw agricultural commodities like Uruguayan linseed oil—to bypass dollar shortages and conserve vital EROA (Economic Rehabilitation in Occupied Areas) funds for non-barterable imports. It also reveals the administrative mechanisms, price comparisons, and jurisdictional boundaries between SCAP, the Department of the Army, and the State Department as international wartime commodity allocation systems (like the IEFC) were being phased out.
overview: This file comprises an incoming Department of State telegram (Army message C-67966 / C-67956) dated February 19, 1949, sent from Tokyo (SCAP) to the Secretary of State regarding the procurement of linseed oil and flaxseed. The telegram reviews prior radio correspondence from December 1948 between SCAP and the Department of the Army (CSCAD BMP) regarding a proposed barter arrangement to exchange Japanese cotton, rayon, and other manufactured goods for 5,000 tons of Uruguayan linseed oil. SCAP reports that negotiations secured a price of $480 per metric ton from Uruguay—substantially lower than the prevailing U.S. market rate of $612.87 ($0.278 per pound)—and contends that failing to finalize the transaction would be unjustifiable, particularly as it would conserve Economic Rehabilitation in Occupied Areas (EROA) appropriated funds for other essential commodities. SCAP requests immediate comments from the State Department and the Department of Agriculture.

subfiles.about: SCAP reports on negotiations to barter Japanese textiles for 5,000 metric tons of Uruguayan linseed oil at $480 per ton and requests immediate comments.
subfiles.summary: This two-page telegram references an exchange of radios from December 1948 between SCAP and the Department of the Army regarding a proposed barter transaction of 5,000 tons of Uruguayan linseed oil in exchange for Japanese cotton and rayon exports. The Department of the Army had indicated no objection to the barter, noting that linseed oil was no longer subject to International Emergency Food Council (IEFC) allocation and that appropriated funds could not be used for reimbursement. SCAP reports that negotiations finalized an offer of $480 per metric ton, which was materially below the U.S. domestic market price of $612.87 ($0.278 per pound). Emphasizing that the barter would conserve EROA funds for other critical commodities, SCAP considers prior communications as authority to proceed and requests immediate comments from Washington.
subfiles.title: Telegram C-67966 from Tokyo (SCAP) to Secretary of State regarding Linseed Oil Barter with Uruguay
